newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia oil workers to "substantially" cut output.
newsitem.headline: Colombia oil workers to "substantially" cut output.

text.p: Colombia's main oil workers' union will be looking to "substantially" cut the country's oil output in the nationwide strike due to begin at midnight Monday (0500 GMT), its leader Hernando Hernandez said.
He declined to give an exact figure but said production and refining activities could be scaled down as much as 50 percent.
"We have sent a directive out to workers calling on them to make every effort to substantially cut back output," Hernandez told Reuters.

The oil workers' union represents about 7,000 employees of the state-run oil company Ecopetrol. A total of about 10,000 oil workers and contractors are expected to heed the strike call, along with an estimated 800,000 other state workers, Hernandez said.
Colombian and foreign private sector oil companies, however, predicted the strike would have little effect on their activities.

Ecopetrol, independently of its private sector associates, currently produces about 411,000 barrels of crude per day and has a daily throughput of about 260,000 at its main refineries in Barrancabermeja and Cartagena.
